_about: Schema + policy for USER-ADDED design rules layered on top of the Envil defaults (IPC_STANDARDS.md / ipc_constraints.json / fab_profiles.json / net_classes.json). Each user (and each project) can add their own rules in plain language; the agent ANALYSES the rule, fills the structured fields below, and add_design_rule persists it. set_design_rules then resolves baseline + user + project into the effective rule set. Pure data + policy — no per-user constants in code.
_model: Layered: Layer0 = Envil defaults (ships). Layer1 = per-user overlay (applies to all that user's boards). Layer2 = per-project overlay (this board only). Precedence at resolve time: PROJECT > USER > DEFAULT. Each user has a different overlay file, so each user gets different rules.

storage._comment: Where overlays live. user overlay = one file per user under user_dir; project overlay = a sidecar next to the .kicad_pro. {user} is replaced by the user_id (default 'default'). Resolved against ENVIL_HOME / the project folder at runtime.
storage.managed_dru_marker: # ENVIL-MANAGED — default (IPC) + user design rules; safe to regenerate

safety_policy._comment: What happens when a user rule is LOOSER than the IPC/fab safety floor. Chosen: warn_but_allow — the user stays in control, but every looser-than-floor rule carries a visible warning the agent must surface. block = reject looser rules. allow_silent = no warning.
safety_policy.warning_template: '{text}' sets {parameter}={value}{unit}, which is LOOSER than the {floor_source} floor of {floor}{unit}. Board may fail DRC/fab. Applied anyway (warn_but_allow).

kinds._comment: A user rule is exactly one of these kinds. The agent picks the kind when it analyses the user's words.
kinds.override: Set a known numeric design-rule parameter (from overridable_parameters below). Floor-checked. e.g. 'my fab min trace is 0.2mm' -> parameter=min_track_width_mm, value=0.2.
kinds.directive: A conditional/spatial rule that maps to a KiCad custom rule (.kicad_dru): a condition + a constraint. e.g. 'keep mains nets 8mm apart' -> condition on netclass, constraint clearance min 8mm. Not floor-checked (it is usually STRICTER).
kinds.selection: Pick a named profile/option: fab_profile, stackup_profile, acceptance_class, copper_weight. e.g. 'I use JLCPCB 4-layer'.
kinds.preference: A non-DRC design preference recorded for the agent to honour (e.g. 'green soldermask', 'SMD on top only', 'label every test point'). Stored + surfaced; no automatic geometry change.

overridable_parameters._comment: Catalog of numeric parameters a user 'override' rule may set. kicad_key = the .kicad_pro board.design_settings.rules key written. fab_key = the fab_profiles.json key whose value is the manufacturing floor. safe_direction='larger' means a BIGGER value is more conservative, so a user value SMALLER than the floor triggers the safety warning (min_* params). 'smaller' is the inverse (none today). Pure data — add a row to allow a new override.

directive_constraints._comment: Constraint types a 'directive' rule may carry, mapped to KiCad .kicad_dru constraint keywords. The agent fills constraint.type + the numeric bound; condition is a KiCad rule condition expression (e.g. "A.NetClass == 'POWER'" or "A.insideArea('bga')"). See IPC_STANDARDS.md §8.

disallow.about: prohibit object type (track/via/hole/zone/footprint) under a condition
